title: Antiderivatives, the FTC & Substitution (Review)
description: Rebuild fluency with antiderivative graphs, integral functions, and u-substitution from the end of Calculus 1.
subskills: Sketch an antiderivative from the graph of f and a given initial value
Differentiate and analyze a function defined by an integral using the Second FTC
Evaluate indefinite integrals by u-substitution
Evaluate definite integrals by u-substitution, changing the limits
prerequisites: MAT 3A S-21, S-22, S-23; chain rule (MAT 3A S-11)

title: Integration by Parts
description: Reverse the product rule to integrate products of functions.
subskills: Choose u and dv and apply the parts formula to an indefinite integral
Apply integration by parts more than once, including integrals that cycle back
Evaluate definite integrals by parts
Decide whether substitution or parts fits a given integral and justify the choice

title: Partial Fractions
description: Integrate rational functions by decomposing them into simpler fractions.
subskills: Decompose a rational function with distinct linear factors
Decompose with repeated linear or irreducible quadratic factors
Integrate each term of a decomposition, using long division first when needed
Evaluate definite integrals of rational functions and interpret the result
prerequisites: S-1; polynomial factoring and long division; ln and arctan antiderivatives (MAT 3A S-12, S-21)

title: Trigonometric Substitution & Integral Tables
description: Use a trigonometric substitution, a table, or technology for integrals outside the basic rules.
subskills: Choose the substitution that matches a^2 - x^2, a^2 + x^2, or x^2 - a^2
Carry out the substitution and return to the original variable with a reference triangle
Match an integral to a table entry, including after a preliminary substitution
Evaluate an integral with technology and check the result by differentiating
prerequisites: S-1; right-triangle trigonometry and identities; MAT 3A S-9

title: Numerical Integration
description: Approximate definite integrals with the Midpoint, Trapezoid, and Simpson's rules and judge their accuracy.
subskills: Compute Midpoint and Trapezoid approximations from a formula, table, or graph
Use concavity to tell whether each rule overestimates or underestimates
Compute a Simpson's rule approximation
Compare errors as n increases and choose n for a required accuracy

title: Area & Arc Length
description: Set up and evaluate integrals for the area between curves and the length of a curve.
subskills: Find the area between curves by integrating with respect to x
Find the area between curves by integrating with respect to y
Set up and evaluate an arc length integral
Explain how a Riemann sum of slices leads to each integral
prerequisites: MAT 3A S-24; S-1; S-5 when no antiderivative exists

title: Volume by Slicing & Disks
description: Find volumes of solids with known cross-sections and solids of revolution using disks.
subskills: Write the volume of a representative slice for a solid with known cross-sections
Set up and evaluate a disk-method integral about the x-axis
Set up and evaluate a disk-method integral about the y-axis
Sketch the region, the solid, and a representative slice
prerequisites: S-6; area formulas for circles, squares, triangles

title: Volume by Washers & Other Axes
description: Find volumes of solids of revolution with holes and solids revolved about other horizontal or vertical lines.
subskills: Identify the outer and inner radius of a representative washer
Set up and evaluate a washer-method integral about a coordinate axis
Set up and evaluate a volume integral about a line such as y = k or x = h
Choose the variable of integration that fits the region and axis

title: Density, Mass & Center of Mass
description: Use definite integrals to find mass from a variable density and to locate a center of mass.
subskills: Find the mass of a rod or region from a density function, with units
Compute the center of mass of a system of point masses
Set up and evaluate integrals for the center of mass of a rod with variable density
Interpret a density function and its integral in context

title: Work, Force & Pressure
description: Use definite integrals to compute work done by a variable force and force from fluid pressure.
subskills: Compute work done by a variable force, including springs (Hooke's Law)
Set up a work integral for pumping liquid from a tank
Set up and evaluate an integral for hydrostatic force on a vertical surface
Track units and explain each factor in the integrand

title: Improper Integrals
description: Evaluate integrals over unbounded intervals or with unbounded integrands, and decide convergence.
subskills: Write an improper integral as a limit of proper integrals
Evaluate improper integrals over infinite intervals
Evaluate improper integrals with a vertical asymptote in the interval
Decide whether an integral converges or diverges, including the family 1/x^p
prerequisites: S-1 through S-3; limits at infinity and L'Hopital's Rule (MAT 3A S-2, S-15)

title: Introduction to Differential Equations
description: Read a differential equation as a statement about a rate of change and test proposed solutions.
subskills: Write a differential equation from a verbal description of a rate
Verify that a function is a solution
Distinguish a general solution from the solution of an initial value problem
Interpret the terms and units of a differential equation in context

title: Slope Fields & Equilibrium Solutions
description: Describe the behavior of solutions qualitatively from a slope field.
subskills: Sketch a slope field for a given differential equation
Sketch solution curves through given initial points
Find equilibrium solutions of an autonomous equation
Classify each equilibrium as stable or unstable

title: Euler's Method
description: Approximate the solution of an initial value problem numerically.
subskills: Carry out Euler's method in a table for a given step size
Explain each step as a tangent-line approximation
Describe how the step size affects the error
Use concavity to decide whether the approximation overestimates or underestimates

title: Separable Differential Equations
description: Solve separable equations and their initial value problems analytically.
subskills: Decide whether a differential equation is separable
Separate variables and integrate to find a general solution
Apply an initial condition and solve explicitly for y when possible
Check a solution by substitution
prerequisites: S-1, S-12; logarithm and exponential algebra

title: Modeling with Differential Equations
description: Build, solve, and interpret models for growth, decay, cooling, and mixing.
subskills: Write a differential equation for a described situation
Solve exponential growth and decay models
Solve a Newton's Law of Cooling or mixing model
Interpret the solution, parameters, and long-term behavior with units

title: Population Growth & the Logistic Equation
description: Analyze and solve the logistic model and compare it with exponential growth.
subskills: Identify the growth rate and carrying capacity in a logistic equation
Find and classify the equilibrium solutions
Solve the logistic equation by separation of variables and partial fractions
Use the solution to predict and compare with an exponential model

title: Taylor Polynomials
description: Extend the tangent line approximation to higher-degree polynomial approximations.
subskills: Find the quadratic approximation of f at x = a
Find the degree-n Taylor polynomial of f centered at a
Use a Taylor polynomial to approximate a function value
Compare approximations of different degrees graphically and numerically

title: Geometric Sums & Series
description: Find finite geometric sums and decide when an infinite geometric series converges.
subskills: Identify the first term and common ratio of a geometric sum
Compute a finite geometric sum with the closed formula
Decide whether an infinite geometric series converges and find its sum
Model a repeated-process situation with a geometric series
prerequisites: Limits at infinity (MAT 3A S-2); exponent rules

title: Taylor Series & Intervals of Convergence
description: Write the Taylor series of a function and determine where it converges.
subskills: Write the Taylor series of f centered at a in sigma notation
Apply the Ratio Test to a series
Find the radius of convergence of a power series
Find the interval of convergence, testing endpoints where the course requires

title: Finding & Using Taylor Series
description: Build new series from known ones and use them to compute.
subskills: Recall the Maclaurin series for e^x, sin x, cos x, and 1/(1 - x)
Find a new series by substitution or multiplication
Differentiate and integrate a power series term by term
Use a series to approximate a definite integral or evaluate a limit

title: Accuracy of Taylor Approximations
description: Bound the error of a Taylor polynomial approximation.
subskills: State the error bound for a degree-n Taylor polynomial
Find a bound M on the (n+1)st derivative over an interval
Bound the error of a given approximation
Find the degree needed to reach a required accuracy

title: Sequences & Convergence Tests for Series
description: Decide whether a sequence or series converges using an appropriate test.
subskills: Find the limit of a sequence or show that it diverges
Apply the Divergence Test and the Integral Test (p-series)
Apply the Comparison and Limit Comparison Tests
Apply the Alternating Series Test and distinguish absolute from conditional convergence

title: Parametric Curves
description: Graph parametric curves and apply calculus to them.
subskills: Sketch a parametric curve and eliminate the parameter
Find dy/dx and the tangent line at a point
Find where the tangent is horizontal or vertical
Set up and evaluate the arc length of a parametric curve

title: Polar Curves
description: Graph polar curves and apply calculus in polar coordinates.
subskills: Convert points and equations between polar and rectangular form
Sketch a polar curve from its equation
Find the slope of a polar curve at a point
Set up and evaluate the area enclosed by a polar curve
